items.followUp: List the main steps involved in solving a computer problem.

rubric.why: Shows the first stages of the problem-solving process.
rubric.description: Names problem definition and problem analysis.

rubric.why: Shows how a solution is planned and carried out.

modelAnswer: The main steps are problem definition, problem analysis, solution design, implementation (coding), testing and debugging, and documentation.

items.followUp: Why is RAM called volatile memory?

rubric.why: Identifies the condition under which stored data is lost.
rubric.description: States that data is lost when the computer is switched off or power is interrupted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying loss of data when power is off.

rubric.why: Explains the meaning of non-volatile memory in contrast to volatile memory.
rubric.description: States that secondary memory retains data without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that secondary memory keeps its data when power is off.

modelAnswer: Secondary memory is called non-volatile memory because it retains stored data even when the computer is switched off or the power supply is interrupted.

rubric.why: Checks the first division and remainder in the decimal-to-hexadecimal conversion.
rubric.description: Correctly divides 357 by 16 and obtains remainder 5.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct first quotient and remainder.
Award 1 mark for the correct hexadecimal answer.

modelAnswer: Read the remainders from bottom to top: (357)₁₀ = (165)₁₆

items.followUp: Draw the truth table for an AND operator.

rubric.why: Checks the output for the case when both inputs are 0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct first row.

rubric.why: Checks the remaining output rows of the OR truth table.
rubric.description: Shows that the output is 1 when either or both inputs are 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct remaining rows.

items.followUp: Write the negation of proposition Q and show its truth table.

rubric.why: Checks the standard notation for the negation of P.
rubric.description: Writes NOT P as ¬P, P′, or NOT P.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct negation notation.

rubric.why: Checks that negation reverses the truth value of P.
rubric.description: Gives the correct truth values for P and NOT P.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct truth table.

modelAnswer: NOT P is written as ¬P (or P′).

items.followUp: Name any two laws of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of a Boolean algebra law.
rubric.description: Names one valid law of Boolean algebra.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct law.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of a second Boolean algebra law.
rubric.description: Names a second valid law of Boolean algebra.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another correct law.

modelAnswer: Two laws of Boolean algebra are the commutative law and the associative law.

items.followUp: State one service that a server computer provides to client computers.

rubric.why: Identifies the server’s role for other computers on a network.
rubric.description: States that a server provides services or shared resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its service/resource role.

rubric.why: Identifies the computers or network that use the server’s services.
rubric.description: States that the services/resources are provided to client computers on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the clients or network.

modelAnswer: A server computer provides services and shared resources, such as files or printers, to client computers on a network.

items.followUp: Define a switch in a computer network.

rubric.why: Checks the router’s role in connecting separate networks.
rubric.description: States that a router connects two or more networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that it connects networks.

rubric.why: Checks how a router directs network traffic.
rubric.description: States that it forwards data packets between networks, typically using IP addresses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing packet forwarding or IP-based routing.

modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that connects two or more networks and forwards data packets between them, using IP addresses to direct the packets.
